blocks.text: Tensor parallelism splits an individual weight matrix, and the matrix multiplication that uses it, across multiple devices, working within a single layer rather than assigning whole layers to different devices the way the simple model parallelism covered in the previous topic does.

This finer grained splitting requires much more frequent communication between devices than layer level splitting, which is why tensor parallelism typically needs a very fast connection between devices to work efficiently, a distinction explored throughout this topic.
1. What Tensor Parallelism Means Specifically

blocks.alt: A single layer gets split within itself, across devices

blocks.text: Rather than assigning entire layers to different devices, tensor parallelism divides the computation inside one single layer, splitting a weight matrix into pieces that different devices each hold and compute with in parallel, before the results get combined back together.
2. Splitting a Single Matrix Multiplication

blocks.alt: A weight matrix splits into column chunks, held by different devices

blocks.text: A common approach splits a weight matrix by columns, giving each device a portion of the columns, each device then computes its own partial result using its chunk, and those partial results get combined to produce the same final output the full, unsplit matrix multiplication would have produced.

code.content:
# A conceptual sketch of column-split tensor parallelism
partial_output_device1 = input_data @ weight_chunk_device1
partial_output_device2 = input_data @ weight_chunk_device2
full_output = concatenate([partial_output_device1, partial_output_device2])

blocks.text: 3. Why Split Within a Layer, Not Across Layers

blocks.alt: Model parallelism splits whole layers while tensor parallelism splits within a layer

blocks.text: The layer level model parallelism covered in the previous topic works well when a model has many layers to distribute, but for models with especially large individual layers, splitting within one layer, as tensor parallelism does, can be necessary even when the total layer count would not otherwise require splitting across devices at all.

blocks.text: 4. Communication Requirements of Tensor Parallelism

blocks.alt: Partial results from device one and device two get combined

blocks.text: Because the partial results from each device chunk of the weight matrix need to be combined before the layer computation is genuinely complete, tensor parallelism requires communication between devices at every split point within a layer, far more frequent than the simple layer boundary communication covered in the previous topic.
5. Tensor Parallelism vs Pipeline Parallelism

blocks.alt: Tensor parallelism needs frequent communication while pipeline parallelism, covered next, needs less frequent communication

blocks.text: Pipeline parallelism, covered in the next topic of this module, splits the model into sequential stages with communication only at stage boundaries, less frequent than tensor parallelism inner layer communication, a tradeoff between the two techniques worth understanding before choosing one for a specific setup.
6. Tensor Parallelism and High Speed Interconnects

blocks.alt: A slow interconnect is compared against a fast, high bandwidth interconnect

blocks.text: Given how frequently devices need to communicate under tensor parallelism, it works best when devices are connected through a very fast, high bandwidth link, and performs poorly if that connection is slow, making the physical hardware setup, not just the software configuration, a genuine factor in whether tensor parallelism makes sense for a given situation.

blocks.title: This connects to the GPU Fundamentals discussion of memory bandwidth
blocks.content: Just as memory bandwidth within a single GPU matters for feeding its cores efficiently, covered in the GPU Fundamentals topic, the bandwidth of the connection between multiple GPUs matters just as much for tensor parallelism to work well.

blocks.text: 7. A Concrete Attention Layer Example

blocks.alt: The query projection gets split across attention heads

blocks.text: A natural place to apply tensor parallelism is within the multi-head attention mechanism, covered in the Foundation Models module, splitting different attention heads across different devices, since each head computation is already somewhat independent, making this a relatively clean split point.
8. When Tensor Parallelism Is Worth the Complexity

Tensor parallelism is worth its added complexity and communication overhead specifically for very large models where individual layers themselves are too large to fit comfortably, and when devices genuinely have the fast interconnect needed to make the frequent communication practical rather than a bottleneck.
9. Tensor Parallelism in Practice

Given its complexity, tensor parallelism is typically implemented through established frameworks and libraries, covered further in the Fine-Tuning Frameworks module later in this course, rather than built from scratch, since correctly splitting and recombining matrix operations across devices is genuinely intricate to get right.
Worked Example

A team fine-tuning an extremely large model finds that even individual layers are too large to fit on a single device, a problem simple layer level model parallelism alone cannot solve since it assumes whole layers fit somewhere.

Using tensor parallelism to split the weight matrices within their largest layers across multiple devices connected through a fast interconnect, they successfully fit and train the model, accepting the frequent inter-device communication as a necessary cost given their model genuinely requires this finer grained splitting.
Common Mistakes

items: Attempting tensor parallelism over a slow network connection, causing communication overhead to dominate training time
Reaching for tensor parallelism when simpler layer level model parallelism would have been sufficient
Implementing tensor parallelism from scratch rather than relying on established, well tested framework support
Confusing tensor parallelism's within-layer splitting with pipeline parallelism's across-layer staging, covered in the next topic

blocks.text: Practice

In your own words, explain why tensor parallelism requires more frequent inter-device communication than the simple layer level model parallelism covered in the previous topic, and why that makes fast device interconnects so important for it to work well.
Key Takeaway

Tensor parallelism splits the computation within a single layer, dividing a weight matrix across devices and combining their partial results, a finer grained approach than simple layer level model parallelism that requires much more frequent inter-device communication, making it best suited to setups with very large individual layers and fast, high bandwidth connections between devices.
